title: Prose playbook: component contracts and runbook for token/button/table/chart migrations
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a prose-led playbook and operational runbook for migrating consumer-facing docs from legacy component primitives to the new component contracts. The playbook will prioritize tokens, primary/secondary button families, compact/table surfaces, and chart config patterns. Goal is to produce easy-to-read migration steps, copy-focused examples, verification checks, and a small set of canonical code snippets that can be embedded in the docsite interactive examples.
scope: Include: design rationale, API contract differences, do/don't guidance, copy-first examples for tokens/buttons/tables/charts
Include: step-by-step migration runbook for engineers and product designers (checklist + quick commands)
Include: acceptance tests and QA checklist for visual regressions and accessibility
Exclude: full API reference generation for all components (this ticket will link to generated API but not re-author it)
acceptance_criteria: A single prose playbook page exists in the docsite with sections for tokens, buttons, tables, charts
Each section has a two-column example: "Before" (legacy usage) and "After" (new contract) with copy explaining trade-offs
Migration runbook includes a 6-step checklist that an engineer can follow and a one-command snippet for updating tokens via codemod
QA checklist includes visual diff thresholds, keyboard interaction checks, and ARIA attribute verification
Design sign-off from Alix Moreno and engineering sign-off from Omar Singh recorded in comments
migration_notes: Tokens: map legacy token names to semantic tokens (e.g., legacy-gray-600 -> surface-muted); provide JSON mapping and codemod link
Buttons: standardize on the new 'intent' prop (primary/secondary/tertiary) instead of style-variants; note subtle padding and focus-ring changes and how to opt into legacy spacing for a short window
Tables: adopt compact row-heights by default; explain column-resize contract change and new onColumnResize callback shape
Charts: move from style overloading to config-driven theming; list required fields that changed (colorScale -> paletteName, margin -> insetPadding) and conversion examples
Codemod: include sample npx command and target patterns for token and button prop renames
Rollout: recommend canary route for high-impact components (buttons/tables) and full rollout for tokens after 2-week smoke period
examples:
Tokens - Before:
Label
Tokens - After:
Label
(semantic token)

Button - Before: <Button variant="ghost">Save</Button>
Button - After: <Button intent="primary">Save</Button> (intent-driven UI)

Table - Before: <Table compact="false">...
Table - After: <Table density="compact">... (new density API)

Chart - Before: <LineChart colors="[\"#aaa\",\"#bbb\"]" />
Chart - After: <LineChart theme="brand" /> (uses paletteName)
Link to interactive sandbox: https://docsite.redwood.ai/sandbox/migration-playbook (embedded live snippets)
do_dont: Do: Prefer semantic tokens for UI intent rather than surface-level color names
Don't: Perform a global token rename without a codemod and smoke tests — this will break computed styles in customer apps
Do: Use intent prop for buttons to keep spacing and focus consistent across themes
Don't: Mix legacy button variants with the new intent API on the same page during rollout
Do: Run visual-diff tests against the released canary before wider rollout
Don't: Skip ARIA and keyboard checks for table row actions — column-resize impacts focus order
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): release tokens and button intent mapping to 5% of traffic; create monitoring dashboard for click/keyboard regressions
Phase 2 (expand): after 7 days with no regressions, roll buttons to 50% and run cross-team demo with Integrations and Platform teams
Phase 3 (wide): full rollout for tokens and charts after 14 days and automated codemod applied to internal repos
Fallback: maintain legacy component variants behind a feature flag for 30 days with automatic fallback policy configured
